rows.38:0900:
Hi, everyone.
I'm Reiko Fukuzawa.
A first-yeeear!
Please be sweet to me-e-e-e!
This is out of nowhere, but do you all like flowers?{p}How about you, {c}{f:|}? Do you like them?
rows.38:09d0:
Oh!
You said you like them.
Hee hee hee... Don't blame me for what happens to you later.
So, {c}{f:|}?
What about cherry blossoms in particular?{p}I bet you just love cherry blossoms.
rows.38:0a94:
Aren't you panicking a little?
You actually like them, but you got worried and said you hate them, didn't you?
Honestly, it's too late to say you hate them now.
What you said about liking flowers was heard loud and clear.
By who?
You're asking who heard it?
The flower spirits.{p}
rows.38:0b90:
Ah, you laughed just now, didn't you?
You've got a look on your face that says being overheard by something like that doesn't scare you one bit.
Well, whatever.
The one who'll be in trouble later is you anyway, {c}{f:|}.
Believe it or don't, that's up to you...{p}
rows.38:0c68:
Flowers and trees, you see, have spirits living in them.
Especially trees that are hundreds or thousands of years old.
They've seen all kinds of history, right?
How people lived, how towns changed over time... they've seen all sorts of things.
They're way greater than humans, you know.
Are you making fun of me?
You think I'm weird, don't you?
Flowers, you know, understand human words.
And not just words.
They even understand feelings.
It's been proven in experiments with cacti, you know.
Cacti grow faster or slower depending on what people say to them, and they even bloom with more beautiful flowers.
I keep little cactus pals too.
Two cactus cuties named Taro and Hanako.
I talk to them every day.
That's what's important, you know.
If you talk to them gently and raise them with care, they grow into that much finer cactus pals.
So, the reverse is true too.
If you curse at them, show them nasty sights, neglect them, or treat them roughly... even plants get angry.
Especially trees like the ones I mentioned, that have lived for hundreds or thousands of years. They're scary when you make them angry.
Because spirits live in them.{p}
rows.38:1044:
So, {c}{f:|}, you've seen it too, right?
The one big cherry tree behind the old school building.
That lone tree, standing all by itself, lonely, as if it's been forgotten for some reason.
They say that cherry tree is over a thousand years old.
That's why it's so huge.
And to tell you the truth, the second athletic field behind the new school building was supposed to be built over there.
But it couldn't be, because of that cherry tree.
Do you know why?{p}
rows.38:11bc:
They say whenever someone tries to cut down that cherry tree or dig it up, accidents happen.
Apparently three people died during the construction.
The one who tried to chop the tree down was crushed to death under a steel beam.
The two who tried to dig it up each came down with a fever no one could explain, and after suffering for a week, hovering between life and death, they died.
Nobody can lay a hand on it.
Moving it somewhere else doesn't work either, apparently.
Purification rites, anything they tried, nothing worked at all.{p}
rows.38:138c: Oh, they heard what you just said too, you know.{p}Then how about you try chopping down that cherry tree?
rows.38:13e8: I can't do something like that
rows.38:1418:
Right.
Of course you couldn't do something that terrifying.
Phew, what a relief.
If you'd dragged out an axe from somewhere and said we should go chop it down right now, I don't know what I would have done.
I might have run away.
I'm glad you've got at least a shred of common sense, {c}{f:|}.{p}
rows.38:1544:
But hey, aren't you curious?
About that cherry tree.
Trees are smart, so a tree that grew up normally won't get angry or get in the way, as long as you make it understand the situation.
Haven't you heard other stories about trees that curse you when you try to cut them down?
With those, it's one or the other: either nobody properly explained the situation to the tree, or an evil spirit lives in it.
That's what I think.
And with that cherry tree, they did properly explain the situation to it.
They even told it they were only moving it somewhere else, and they'd never hurt it.
That's what I heard, anyway.{p}
rows.38:171c: But since it wouldn't accept that, there really must be an evil spirit living in it.{p}Do you think there's an evil spirit living in that cherry tree too?
rows.38:17b4:
I see.
So that's what you think.{p}
rows.38:17dc:
Maybe you don't believe the stories about the people who had those accidents, either?
If so, that's scary.
You're definitely going to get cursed, {c}{f:|}.
But you know, there really are all kinds of bad rumors about that cherry tree.
I'll tell you about them.
...It's a story from decades and decades ago, though.{p}
rows.38:18f0:
They say that during the war, the area around that cherry tree was used as a dumping ground for corpses.
The rumor is they dug a pit and threw the bodies into it. Scary story, right?
And not just dead bodies, either. People who were still breathing but had no hope of being saved got thrown in too, without mercy.
So it was a picture of hell, literally.
They kept dumping bodies one after another, right?
They couldn't fill in the pit until it was full, so the stench of rotting flesh was unbelievable.
They say even if you only watched from far away, the smell came drifting over on the wind.
And drifting along with it came the moans of the living, sorrowful and full of hatred and grudges.
"It hurts..."
and
"I'm in agony..."
and not only that, but voices so full of hatred they weren't even words anymore kept coming out of that pit without a break.
Twenty-four hours a day, nonstop.{p}
rows.38:1c6c:
That's torture, isn't it?
In its thousand years of life, it was probably the most horrifying sight it had ever seen.
Just try watching a sight like that, on and on.
If you were human, you'd go mad, of course.
And this is a plant, full of emotions.
When I think about how it must have felt, I can't help feeling sorry for it.
And on top of that, it's been living by feeding on those people, right?{p}
rows.38:1dc0:
The people who died cursing the war and cursing humanity slowly rotted away to nothing and became one with the soil.
That tree has been living by sucking up their juices.
The people dumped there must have returned not only their flesh but even their souls to the earth.
So that cherry tree has sucked up the grudges of hundreds of people.
Next time, you should take a good look.
If you stare at it, faces of people writhing in agony will rise up on that great tree's trunk.
The knots in the wood look like that, you see.
That's no coincidence.
Without a doubt, it's the piled-up grudges of the countless dead.
Those grudges get carved into the trunk like that, one after another.{p}
rows.38:2024:
If you think I'm lying, shall we go check right now?
I can see them, after all.
You should definitely be able to see them too.
Right?{p}Won't you come?
rows.38:21a0:
Look, that tree.
That cherry tree.
After hearing what I just told you, doesn't it look even creepier somehow?
Hey, you kind of get that feeling, right?
Come on, get closer.
Get right up next to it and take a good look.{p}
rows.38:2268:
...That's it.
...Like you're going to lick it.
Well?
Can you see them?
The faces of the people who died holding grudges.
Don't you see lots of them?
These hollows around here are too perfect to be a coincidence, aren't they?
After all, it sucked up the blood of so many people.
After all, it sucked up the souls of so many people.
Even now, their bones are buried right under here.
Can you see them?{p}Did you see them?
rows.38:23bc:
That's strange.
And you seem like you'd have a strong sixth sense, {c}{f:|}.
Get even closer.
So close your body is pressed right up against it.{p}
rows.38:243c:
Smell it too.
Mixed in with the fresh green smell of the tree, don't you smell something weird?
Something like sulfur.
A smell like rotten eggs.
A smell like burning corpses.
Right?
Don't you sense it?
Are you starting to see them?{p}Still can't see them?
rows.38:2518:
That's strange...
There's no way you can't see them.
Put your hand on the trunk.
...That's it.
You'll definitely be able to see them, I know it.
Bring your face closer.
Closer, closer...{p}
rows.38:2624:
If you still can't see them after this, that proves your sixth sense is weak.
And if you did see them...
Ahahahaha...
Well then, shall we head back to the club room?
We have to hear the next person's story, too.{p}
rows.38:27bc:
My mom's family home is in a place famous for its cherry blossoms.
In mid-April, the rows of cherry trees that stretch for kilometers along the embankment all bloom at once.
When the blossoms are falling, they're so beautiful there's just no way to describe it.
When you walk through a storm of cherry petals, you get so elated it's like you're flying through the air.
When I was little, standing in the middle of it all, I honestly used to believe that my body was made of cherry petals, and that I'd be blown away on the wind with the falling blossoms and vanish.{p}
rows.38:2968:
It's not just flowers that I love.
My room is full of houseplants.
Like a jungle.
Maybe it's because plants really are alive.
If I look after them every day, talk to them and love them, they always give those feelings back to me.
They bloom with beautiful flowers, they ease my stress, and they grow up super healthy.
And they sense my emotions really keenly and react to them, too.
When I'm sick or worried about something, the flowers droop right away and lose their energy.{p}
rows.38:2b50:
Aren't they cute?
Aren't they sweet?
I'll say it straight: I think plants have feelings.
Some people say that's because spirits live in them.
They say trees that have lived hundreds or thousands of years are scary when you make them angry, right?
So your answer to my question earlier was heard loud and clear by the spirits, too.
From now on, if you say anything too weird, don't blame me for whatever happens to you later.{p}
rows.38:2cc0:
Hmm, you don't seem very interested.
Well, fine.
This is out of nowhere, but how do you feel when you look at cherry blossoms?
Have you ever walked through that storm of petals when the cherry blossoms are falling?
It's spectacular, isn't it?{p}
rows.38:2d60:
You say you neither like nor hate flowers, but what about that?
Don't you ever feel good when you look at cherry blossoms?
Don't you ever think, 'How beautiful'?
{f:Geez|Hmm}, {f:you're so wishy-washy|you've got me stumped}.{p}
rows.38:2ec4:
By the flower spirits.
Didn't you know?{p}
